name: Node.js
shortDescription: Node.js runs JavaScript outside a web browser. Learn to read a file and write small programs. Use a separate Node.js tool to try these lessons.

name: Express.js
shortDescription: Express is a small Node.js tool for handling web requests and sending replies. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: NestJS
shortDescription: NestJS organises a Node.js server into controllers, modules and shared services. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.
highlights: Send a client to another route

name: Fastify
shortDescription: Fastify is a Node.js web framework with useful tools for route schemas, plugins and request tests. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Django
shortDescription: Django is a Python web framework with routing, views, forms and data tools. These first lessons focus on simple views. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Flask
shortDescription: Flask is a small Python web framework. It connects URL routes to Python functions. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: FastAPI
shortDescription: FastAPI is a Python framework for web APIs. Type hints help it check inputs and describe routes. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Spring Framework
shortDescription: Spring Framework can create and connect objects for a Java program. Its container looks after these shared objects, called beans. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Spring Boot
shortDescription: Spring Boot starts a Spring application with ready-made defaults. These lessons build tiny HTTP endpoints without a database. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: ASP.NET Core
shortDescription: ASP.NET Core is a .NET tool for websites and APIs. Minimal APIs let a small function handle a web request. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: ASP.NET Web API
shortDescription: A Web API sends data to other programs. ASP.NET Core controllers group the request actions into C# classes. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Laravel
shortDescription: Laravel is a PHP framework with routing, response helpers and collections. These first lessons work with small web replies. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.
highlights: Build a URL from a name

name: Symfony
shortDescription: Symfony is a PHP framework built from reusable components. These lessons use its routes, requests and response objects. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Ruby on Rails
shortDescription: Rails is a Ruby framework with clear places for routes and controllers. These API-only examples return small data replies. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Gin
shortDescription: Gin is a Go web framework. Its context object helps read request data and write replies. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: Fiber
shortDescription: Fiber is a Go web framework with a compact request context. These lessons use its stable v2 API. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.
highlights: Read a body into a struct

name: Phoenix
shortDescription: Phoenix is an Elixir web framework. It uses a router, controllers and a connection value to handle requests. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: GraphQL
shortDescription: GraphQL lets a client ask for specific fields of data. A schema describes what can be asked for. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: REST API Development
shortDescription: A REST-style API names resources with URLs and uses HTTP methods to read or change them. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: WebSockets
shortDescription: WebSockets keep a two-way connection open so either side can send messages without a fresh HTTP request. Start with 12 small lessons, clear examples and practice questions.

name: C# .NET and Oracle Backend
shortDescription: Build a small Reading List API with C#, .NET 10 and Oracle. Use simple lessons, a downloadable project, safe SQL parameters and real create, read, update and delete requests.
highlights: Build one complete local backend project
Connect C# to an Oracle book table
Test requests and add a small browser page
